::: {.why}
Non-stationarity is the failure mode that no cross-validation scheme catches, because every scheme assumes the thing being estimated is the same thing throughout.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report how much your fitted relationship varies across eras, and say whether that variation is larger than estimation error.
- Say what a model should do about non-stationarity, and why the obvious answer of a shorter window has a cost you can quantify.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Test formally rather than by eye: for each coefficient, compare the across-era variance against the within-era standard errors. If the first exceeds the second, the relationship is genuinely moving and a single fitted model is estimating an average of different things.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Quantify the window trade-off: fit the model on rolling windows from 1 to 10 years and plot the out-of-sample R-squared against window length. A short window adapts and has more estimation error; a long window is stable and stale. The maximum of that curve is your answer and it is a measurement rather than a preference.
:::
:::
